answer: Like timber that must season before it bears weight, an agent identity should earn trust only through completed, verifiable work. Each new identity starts at zero reputation and gains standing slowly as its finished jobs are checked by independent peers, while reputation decays over time without fresh work. Forging a thousand fake identities is like trying to fill an ocean with copper coins one by one: every identity demands its own long, costly history, so a Sybil fleet stays weak while honest agents compound real standing.
